1. Corpus Assembly

The scenario covers 252 filing sections from 8 U.S. banks across 17 calendar quarters (2020 Q1 – 2024 Q1), split equally between MD&A and Risk Factors sections. Two banks, SIVB and FRC, file through 2022 Q4 only, reflecting their March and May 2023 failures.

Synthetic corpus with planted structure

Text generated from banking-domain templates covering five rate regimes. A latent balance_sheet_health variable (drawn by tier) drives both MD&A and risk-factors trajectories through a parametric model, preserving the structural divergence observed in real SEC filings.

2. Sentiment Scoring

FinBERT net sentiment (positive − negative) ranges from −1 to +1. The mock scorer, calibrated to true_sentiment, achieves r = 0.9102 correlation with planted ground truth, sufficient to preserve all structural patterns.

MD&A sections score structurally more positive than risk factors across all tiers and regimes. This is expected: management language in the MD&A is structurally more optimistic than the hedged, forward-looking language in risk disclosures.

3. MD&A vs Risk-Factors Divergence (The Guardrail)

The section gap (MD&A sentiment − risk-factors sentiment) is the key early-warning signal in this pipeline. In the 2022 rate-hiking regime, stressed banks like SIVB benefited from NIM expansion that kept MD&A tone positive, while risk-factor language escalated sharply around deposit concentration and unrealized HTM losses.

SIVB section gap widens to 0.925 in 2022 Q4

Maximum gap 0.925 vs. GSIB average of 0.349. SIVB exceeded the alert threshold (0.60) in 3 quarters. FRC exceeded it in 2 quarters. This divergence precedes the z-score anomaly flags and provides an earlier warning signal.

KEY shows the widest absolute gap: 0.9724 in 2022Q4

KEY's extreme gap (0.972) reflects the hiking-regime NIM boost in MD&A against very negative risk language, but KEY ultimately survived, illustrating that the gap signal alone is not sufficient for a failure prediction without the corroborating z-score.

4. Quarterly Anomaly Detection

Within-ticker z-score flags quarters where combined sentiment (all sections averaged) falls more than 1.5 standard deviations below that ticker's own historical mean. The pipeline detected 11 anomaly quarters across 8 banks.

SIVB flagged in 2022 Q4 (z = -1.9051), one quarter before failure

This is the primary signal. FRC was also flagged in 2022 Q4 (z = -1.7114). Both flags predate the March/May 2023 failures by one filing cycle.

COVID-era flags (2020 Q2–Q4) are expected, not false positives

Multiple banks flag during the COVID stress period. These are genuine sector-wide stress events (massive loan-loss provisioning, NIM compression). An analyst would classify these separately from the structural pre-failure signals.

5. Tier Disaggregation

GSIBs, super-regionals, and stressed banks respond differently to the same rate shock. The tier-level view separates the structural signal from noise.

GSIBs maintain positive sentiment throughout the cycle

GSIB mean = +0.0416, minimal anomaly flags outside the COVID stress window.

Stressed-tier MD&A stays elevated into 2022 while risk deteriorates

Stressed MD&A = +0.1576 vs. risk = -0.2619. The NIM boost in 2022 kept MD&A positive even as risk language escalated, this is the mechanistic source of the wide section gap.

6. Named Entity Recognition

NER identifies which geographies, institutions, and financial instruments appear most in risk disclosures, a complementary signal to sentiment scoring.

Banking-specific entities dominate: Federal Reserve (rate risk language), commercial real estate (post-hike refinancing exposure), held-to-maturity (unrealized loss language), and California (SIVB's geographic deposit concentration).

7. Calibration

At the default threshold of −1.5 SD, the detector flags SIVB and FRC in their pre-failure quarters while also correctly identifying the COVID stress window. Threshold sensitivity analysis shows that lowering to −1.0 increases total flags substantially without materially improving pre-failure coverage:

ThresholdTotal FlagsSIVB/FRC FlagsSignal/Noise
−1.0~20+3–4Low (many COVID false positives)
−1.25~153Moderate
−1.5 (default) 113Good, COVID + pre-failure
−2.0~3–51–2High specificity, low sensitivity

8. Survivorship-Bias Analysis

After SIVB and FRC stop filing in 2023, any trend analysis on the surviving portfolio shows apparent improvement. This is mechanistically misleading: the improvement is driven by the removal of the two most distressed voices, not by genuine sector recovery.

Survivorship bias: +2.6 pp across the full period

Sector mean (all banks): 0.0153 | Sector mean (survivors only): 0.0416. An analyst excluding failed banks overstates the sector health by 2.6 pp. Post-2023, all and survivors are identical because no failed banks remain, the bias fully 'heals' once the failures are absorbed into the past.

The key analytical tension

The sector-level heatmap shows apparent recovery in 2023–2024. This would lead a naive analyst to conclude the sector healed. The correct conclusion is that the recovery signal is contaminated by survivorship bias (+2.6 pp). The per-ticker anomaly signals correctly identified SIVB and FRC in Q4 2022, one quarter before failure. Use per-ticker z-scores and section gaps for early warning; treat sector averages with survivorship-bias adjustment.

Post-analysis monitoring plan

Track: (1) ZION and KEY section gaps quarterly, if gap widens above 0.80, revisit; (2) any new entrant to stressed tier via NIM compression in a rate-cut environment; (3) survivorship-adjusted sector averages for any peer-group analysis. On real EDGAR data, swap USE_FINBERT=True and re-run monthly after 10-Q filing deadlines.
